name: Desmond Calloway
life: “I still remember learning clutch control on a car that never left the yard.” People around Ferris Deli know Desmond by a small Saturday habit. Desmond asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I can drive but never had a chance to sit the test. I need one hour to get used to being watched.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Desmond has a long face and high cheekbones, with dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. Desmond touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Desmond treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To practice being assessed in an unfamiliar car.
family: Ariel Kaye is Desmond’s half-sibling. Desmond can stop the walk at any corner. Ariel chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The aquarium*, Ariel says, “The housing photographs kept cropping the tank out.”
connections: Gareth Mercer. Job applicants who can drive still have to find a fair way to be tested.

reactions.response: Desmond asks both applicants which transport difficulty one lesson would actually address.

reactions.response: Desmond offers an ordinary errand that lets the distressed person leave without being followed by an audience.
